summary: Reproduced the benchmark endpoint's inherited accelerator-context failure on the assigned gfx950 GPU and changed only the outer server process to use an explicit spawn context. Added a failing-before/passing-after process-context regression and independent reuse/connect boundary tests.

tests.what_was_measured: The new regression rejected the default fork path because multiprocessing.get_context('spawn') was not called; the two independent reuse/connect boundary tests passed. Raw output: reports/j-67eb4114c75c/raw/unit_before.txt

All three focused tests passed: explicit spawn for launch, no process creation when reusing a live server, and no launch when an explicit base URL is supplied. Raw output: reports/j-67eb4114c75c/raw/unit_after.txt

After the parent initialized ROCm, the forked child failed its real GPU allocation with 'Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess'; launch_or_reuse_server reported the child exit. Raw output: reports/j-67eb4114c75c/raw/repro_before.txt

After parent ROCm initialization, the spawned child independently allocated a GPU tensor, computed 7.0, and was alive when the endpoint became ready. Raw output: reports/j-67eb4114c75c/raw/repro_final.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950:sramecc+:xnack- was used with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015. Inventory is in reports/j-67eb4114c75c/raw/gpu_inventory.txt; before/after allocation evidence is in repro_before.txt and repro_after.txt.

remaining_limitations: No Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B weights were available, so no full model startup or semantic inference was run.
The fixture validates the benchmark endpoint process boundary and real ROCm accelerator execution only; it does not qualify multimodal image preprocessing or a distributed workload.
NVIDIA CUDA and Intel XPU hardware were unavailable, so those vendor-specific paths were not executed.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
